mechanism_narrative: The steady week-to-week decline in negative WORKPLACES mobility means more people are returning to commuting and adjacent errands. That activity should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, with the effect appearing after a short lag as workplace-return routines spill into shopping trips.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues moving toward baseline but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility drops toward baseline from its elevated level, time spent at home is shrinking and discretionary out-of-home activity should shift toward retail locations. This should lift RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks after the residential decline becomes material.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1.5 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not rise within the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates both commuting and in-person activity are recovering together. Their joint strengthening should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks because more trips combine travel and shopping purposes.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the following 28 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT is still far below baseline and deteriorates further, access friction for discretionary trips remains high and retail visits should continue to weaken. The mechanism predicts lower RETAIL_REC over the next month when transit mobility stays severely depressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25 and falls further week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -25 but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An upward break in PARKS mobility after a previously weak level signals households are reallocating discretionary time outdoors. That pattern should precede a short-term lift in RETAIL_REC as park trips and shopping trips cluster in the same out-of-home budget.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from 0 or below to above 0
failure_condition: If PARKS turns positive and RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 7 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated while WORKPLACES continues to recover, essential and commuting trips reinforce each other and create more chance retail exposure. Under that interaction, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next two weeks, not merely stay stable.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above baseline and WORKPLACES improves but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days, reject the interaction.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PARKS alongside a decline in RESIDENTIAL indicates more time is being spent outside the home for leisure. In that regime, retail and recreation mobility should strengthen over the following four weeks as outdoor activity broadens discretionary trip chains.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL falls and RETAIL_REC still declines over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If the recent flattening in negative TRANSIT mobility reverses and transit usage turns down again, retail mobility will lag because fewer people will combine errands with trips into the city center. This should lower RETAIL_REC within four weeks after the transit reversal.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stops improving and falls back by at least 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT worsens by at least 2 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
